text:
sara: Heads up — eu-dedicated canary is spiking p95 and tail errors. Deploy bot flagged it.

deploy-bot: automated alert — canary p95 = 720ms (+210ms vs baseline) over 5m window; client_error_rate +3.2%. Suggested action: PAUSE roll and run targeted probe. auto-rollback suppressed (maintenance-window tag).

kevin: Thanks. Did we push the quantization kernel change in this roll? That landed in the runtime branch earlier.

maria: yes that change included kernel switch + small cache hotfix. I ran local perf but not full multi-az canary.

ops_oncall: @sara @kevin @maria — can we get quick diffs between canary vs previous bundle? If kernel change causes tail regen, we may need manual rollback.

jamal: I'm running `redwood telemetry diff --since 10m --channel eu-dedicated --metric p95,errors` now, will share snippet.

jamal: snippet:
```
p95_canary: 720ms
p95_prev: 480ms
error_rate_canary: 1.9%
error_rate_prev: 0.6%
```

maria: hmm error-rate uptick small but p95 regression notable. Any customer-facing errors in logs? Search for HTTP 502/504 spikes.

kevin: quick grep of tails shows a handful of `kv_cache_miss` warnings + one `cuda_sync_timeout` in worker-3.

sara: We have two options: 1) Manual partial rollback of eu pool to v2.3.8 for 50% traffic slice, keep canary pinned; 2) Run a targeted rollback of the runtime kernel flag only (cherry-pick revert) and re-run canary.

ops_oncall: Given maintenance window until 23:00 UTC, automated rollback is disabled. Recommend manual 50% traffic split to reduce blast radius and trigger a new canary evaluation.

deploy-bot: Command templates:
- Split traffic 50% -> `redwood traffic set --pool eu-dedicated --route default --split 50:50 --to v2.3.8,v2.4.0`
- Rollback whole pool -> `redwood rollback --pool eu-dedicated --to v2.3.8`
- Pin canary -> `redwood pin --instance canary-eu --version v2.4.0`

maria: If we do partial rollback we must notify the three enterprise customers on eu-dedicated who requested early access. I'll draft notes.

sara: Decision: execute partial 50% rollback to v2.3.8 now, pin canary, and open a post-mortem if p95 doesn't recover within 20m. @jamal please run the traffic split and monitor.

jamal: executing now: `redwood traffic set --pool eu-dedicated --route default --split 50:50 --to v2.3.8,v2.4.0`

deploy-bot: action started — traffic change requested by jamal. Rollout id: r-606060-01

jamal: applied. monitor stream -> https://telemetry.redwood/prod/eu-dedicated/r-606060-01

kevin: I'll tail logs for `cuda_sync_timeout` and `kv_cache_miss` across both variants. If errors concentrate on v2.4.0 we can isolate kernel revert.

ops_oncall: Notifying SRE rotation and customer success: `@sre-team`, `@cs-eu` — brief: partial rollback in eu-dedicated, holding canary, monitoring. ETA 30m.

maria: Draft to customers: "We've detected latency regression during canary evaluation; we are partially rolling back to reduce impact while we investigate. No data loss expected. We'll update within 30 minutes." OK to send?

sara: Send. Also add link to live monitor and contact for urgency: `ops_oncall`.

jamal: 10m after split: p95 overall dropped to 510ms, error-rate back to 0.7%. v2.3.8 shows p95 490ms, v2.4.0 still ~720ms.

kevin: clear signal. Looks like the runtime kernel path in v2.4.0 is the likely cause. We should prepare a targeted revert of kernel flag and a canary-only redeploy, not a full rollback.

maria: I'll prepare the cherry-pick revert PR for the kernel switch and wire up a quick e2e against canary.

sara: Good. Post-decision checklist:
- [x] Partial traffic rollback applied
- [x] Customers notified
- [x] Live monitor link shared
- [ ] Cherry-pick revert PR (#) + canary redeploy
- [ ] Post-mortem if not resolved in 2 hours

ops_oncall: Keeping this thread open. If anyone wants to escalate to full rollback, add a 👍 by ops lead and ping legal if release notes need revision.

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/release/pull/4321 — request review, CI running. Will redeploy to canary on green.

deploy-bot: canary redeploy scheduled: prometheus health checks will gate rollout. Auto-rollback remains suppressed for this change.

jamal: will monitor and report back every 5 minutes for the next 30.

sara: Thanks team. If canary looks good after revert we can re-roll the remaining traffic and update release notes with the kernel-change rationale.

kevin: also add a line in the release notes about temporary disablement of that kernel toggle and perf validation steps for next rollout.

maria: noted. I'll update release notes in the PR.

ops_oncall: last check at +30m: p95 stable at 485ms, v2.4.0 still showing tail but decreased errors. Keeping partial split for now, continuing investigation.

sara: Closing initial incident action. Will reopen if we see regression. Thanks all. :thumbsup!
